prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Document ingestion environment variables (language en).
Grid: 4 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Name" · longest unbreakable word 377px · one-line width 377px
  col 2: header "Required" · longest unbreakable word 78px · one-line width 78px
  col 3: header "Default" · longest unbreakable word 169px · one-line width 169px
  col 4: header "Description" · longest unbreakable word 172px · one-line width 1212px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 720px. You MAY choose a total wider than 719px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Document the environment variables used to configure document ingestion, including whether each is required, its default, and its meaning.","reading":"Readers scan variable names to find a setting, then read across the row to check its requirement, default, and explanation; they may also compare requirements or defaults down a column.","groups":["Name identifies each row and anchors the corresponding configuration details.","Required and Default are compact configuration properties that readers can scan and compare vertically.","Description explains each variable and benefits most from room for natural prose wrapping."],"keep_intact":["Environment variable names, because they are identifiers readers may copy.","Default values, especially the URL, because they may be copied or interpreted literally.","Required values, including Conditional, so their meaning remains immediately legible."],"may_wrap":["Description prose can wrap at word boundaries; longer descriptions can use the height created when other cells wrap.","If the table must fit the viewport, identifiers or defaults may need to split, though this makes scanning and copying harder."]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r2A: widths [398, 99, 190, 245] · table 933×989px · row heights [36, 153, 129, 106, 129, 153, 129, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 213px
Design r2B: widths [250, 99, 150, 220] · table 720×1105px · row heights [36, 176, 176, 129, 129, 176, 129, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 1
Design r2C: widths [340, 99, 190, 260] · table 890×942px · row heights [36, 153, 129, 106, 106, 129, 129, 153] · column headers wrapped 0/4 · tallest cell 6 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 170px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
